title: row15
live_proof: host ASan on 2026-10-26: heap-use-after-free, an 8-byte READ 8 bytes inside a freed 72-byte region, access sqlite3BtreePager <- sqlite3_backup_step, freed by sqlite3BtreeClose <- detachFunc. Fixed upstream in 3.53.3 by storing db indices and re-deriving the Btree each step.
object: the Btree the backup cached for its source or destination database
lifetime_ender: DETACH on the destination connection closes that database's Btree (attach.c detachFunc -> sqlite3BtreeClose, sqlite3.c:101061), freeing the 72-byte object the backup cached. detachFunc's two guards are sqlite3BtreeIsInReadTrans and sqlite3BtreeIsInBackup; the second reads nBackup, which backup.c increments on p->pSrc ONLY (sqlite3.c:70592), so a backup's DESTINATION is unguarded.
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: the public backup API driven against a connection that DETACHes the backup's destination database mid-backup. Nothing may step the backup before the DETACH -- the first step opens a write transaction on the destination and detachFunc then refuses on sqlite3BtreeIsInReadTrans -- and backup_init has already cached both Btree* through findBtree, which is all the defect needs.

cheribsd-revocation.note: awaiting the 2026-10-29 re-run. The 2026-10-04/05 reading was taken on the broken trigger and is void with the rest (see this case's status). One run was made on the corrected trigger -- 2026-10-26, shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested --only 02, positive-control gate satisfied (exit 162, revocation=1) -- and its SIGPROT is NOT a reading of this mechanism, so no verdict is recorded from it: Host ASan puts the defective access in sqlite3BtreePager, one call earlier; sqlite3PagerSetPagesize is where the pager pointer READ OUT of the freed Btree is used, so this is the consequence and not the rejection. It cannot be revocation either: under memsys5 sqlite3BtreeClose returns the Btree to memsys5's own pool and the platform sees no free, so nothing was revoked. What cleared the tag is memsys5 writing Mem5Link{next,prev} over the freed block's first 8 bytes -- the same mechanism as cases 19 and 20. The run's positive-control gate was satisfied (exit 162, revocation=1).

status: TRIGGER CORRECTED 2026-10-26; EVERY ARM READING BELOW PREDATES IT AND IS VOID. The trigger up to that date did a single ATTACH, which frees nothing in 3.22.0 (attach.c takes sqlite3DbMallocRawNN plus memcpy while db->aDb is still db->aDbStatic), and reallocating db->aDb would not free the cached Btree in any case. Host ASan scored the old trigger SEGV -- the corpus's only SEGV, with no freed-by and no allocated-by chain -- while case.c claimed it reported heap-use-after-free. The arms were scoring a NULL dereference. Re-measurement on every arm is required before any cell here is read again.
fault_sites_why: Host ASan on the corrected trigger reports the stale read in sqlite3BtreePager (sqlite3.c:69480) under sqlite3_backup_step (:70753), an 8-byte read 8 bytes into the freed 72-byte Btree, freed by sqlite3BtreeClose under detachFunc. The former declaration, sqlite3BtreeUpdateMeta, belonged to the broken trigger: nothing was freed there and the fault was a NULL dereference of pBt->pPage1.
